claims.text: The starting material is a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix without added solid lubricants or nanoparticles.
CaF2 nanoparticles can be incorporated as a dispersed phase in the CoCrFeNi matrix during processing.
The incorporated CaF2 phase will be uniformly dispersed.
During sliding, dispersed CaF2 will promote nucleation and stabilization of a continuous lubricious tribofilm.
At lower temperatures, CaF2 nanoparticles will facilitate formation of a thin lubricating film.
The low-temperature lubricating film will minimize direct metal-to-metal contact.
As temperature increases, CaF2 nanoparticles will maintain and renew the tribofilm in oxidizing conditions.
The CaF2-enabled tribofilm will reduce interfacial shear stress.
Adding CaF2 nanoparticles will reduce the coefficient of friction relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C.
Adding CaF2 nanoparticles will reduce wear rate relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C.
The reductions in friction and wear will be statistically significant and consistent across the full temperature range.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi typically exhibits increased friction and wear-rate variability as temperature changes.
The proposed performance benefit is expected in ambient air between 25 °C and 800 °C under moderate, controlled sliding loads and speeds.
The magnitude of friction and wear reduction may depend on CaF2 content and processing conditions.
